To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the present data allow to reconstruct the neutrino matrix in the flavor basis, in case of inverted hierarchy, with some restrictions; (ii) in the case of the inverted hierarchy, the present data do not allow to reconstruct the mass matrix uniquely; (iii) there exist several types of mass matrix structures, which are realized for various values of phases; (iv) the mass matrix elements can correlate with flavor: normal partial and/or complete alignment is possible; (v) the mass
the neutrino mass and flavor data admit the existence of various structures in the mass matrix, which can be realized for particular values of the CP violating phases.

the present data allow for a variety of structures of the neutrino mass matrices, including hierarchical structures with a small set of small (and/or zero) elements, equalities among various group of elements, and ``democratic'' structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the question of how much the neutrino mass matrices can be constrained, given the present data, and how much freedom is still allowed.
the reconstruction of neutrino mass matrix for the inverted mass hierarchy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mass matrix is completely reconstructed only if the absolute scale of masses is determined, and the Majorana phase is measured, and only for a particular structure of the mass matrix, which can be realized in a particular case.
the neutrino mass matrices in flavor basis, for inverted hierarchy, are not unique.

the present neutrino data admit various structures and symmetries for the mass matrix, and the freedom in the matrix elements can be significantly reduced by future measurements of absolute neutrino mass and CP violation in neutrino oscillations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present data allow a wide range of possibilities for the neutrino mass matrices.
, for the inverted mass ordering, the neutrino mass matrices can exhibit various structures, and that these structures can be correlated with the CP violating phases.
the mass matrix in the case of IH can have various structures, which depend strongly on the values of the CP violating phases and on the absolute scale of neutrino masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrino mass matrices in the inverted ordering case can be very different from those for normal ordering.
the neutrino mass and mixing pattern can be reconstructed completely, in particular, in the case when inverted mass hierarchy and CP violation are realized.
the neutrino mass matrices in inverted hierarchy can be very different from the matrices in normal hierarchy.
